title: 黄鹤楼
author: 崔颢
intro: A legend of an immortal who flew away on a yellow crane, a tower left behind, and a traveller at sunset wondering where home is — a poem Li Bai himself is said to have admired too much to compete with.
analysis: 黄鹤楼在今天的武汉，长江边上。传说古代有仙人在这里骑着黄鹤飞走了。诗的前四句从传说写起：仙人早已乘黄鹤离去，这里只留下一座空空的黄鹤楼；黄鹤一去再也没回来，只有白云千百年来悠悠飘荡。“黄鹤”三次出现，“空”字两次出现，打破了律诗不重复用字的规矩，读起来却像民歌一样自然流畅，写出人去楼空、时光流逝的感慨。后四句回到眼前：晴朗的江面上，对岸汉阳的树木一棵棵看得清清楚楚，鹦鹉洲上芳草茂盛。天快黑了，诗人望向远方：我的家乡在哪里呢？江上烟雾茫茫，让人发愁。从神话写到现实，从怀古写到思乡，情和景结合得非常好。传说李白登上黄鹤楼，看到这首诗后说：“眼前有景道不得，崔颢题诗在上头。”南宋严羽称它为唐人七言律诗第一。
analysisEn: Yellow Crane Tower stands on the Yangtze in today’s Wuhan. Legend says an immortal once flew away from here on a yellow crane. The first four lines start from that story: the immortal left long ago on his crane, and all that remains is an empty tower; the crane is gone and never came back, and for a thousand years only white clouds have drifted by. “Yellow crane” appears three times and “empty/only” (空) twice — breaking the rule that a regulated poem shouldn’t repeat characters — yet it flows as naturally as a folk song, and the repetition drives home the feeling of people gone, a building left, time slipping away. The last four lines come back to the present: across the sunlit river every tree in Hanyang is clear to see, and fragrant grass grows thick on Parrot Island. As the sun sets the poet looks into the distance and asks: where is my home? Mist and waves on the river only make him sadder. The poem moves from myth to reality and from the past to his own homesickness, with scene and feeling woven together. Li Bai is said to have climbed the tower, read this poem on the wall, and sighed that there was a view he couldn’t write about, because Cui Hao had already done it. The Song critic Yan Yu called it the finest seven-character regulated poem of the Tang.
background: Cui Hao (c. 704–754) was a Tang poet; few of his poems survive, but this one made him famous. The story of Li Bai declining to write about the tower after reading it is traditional and may be a legend.
pronunciation: 乘 chéng；千载 zǎi（年，不读 zài；机器朗读可能读错，已在“朗读用字”换成同音字“宰”）；萋萋 qī qī；鹦鹉 yīng wǔ；使人愁 shǐ。
version: 采用统编教材（八年级上册）文本。首句有异文“昔人已乘白云去”（不少学者认为是原貌），网站用教材的“乘黄鹤去”；“芳草萋萋”一作“春草萋萋”。

lines.py: xī rén yǐ chéng huáng hè qù
lines.lit: The man of old has already ridden the yellow crane away;
lines.en: The immortal flew off long ago on his yellow crane;

lines.py: cǐ dì kōng yú huáng hè lóu
lines.lit: this place has only the Yellow Crane Tower left, empty.
lines.en: here nothing is left but the Yellow Crane Tower.

lines.py: huáng hè yī qù bù fù fǎn
lines.lit: The yellow crane, once gone, never returns;
lines.en: The crane, once gone, has never come back;

lines.py: bái yún qiān zǎi kōng yōu yōu
lines.lit: white clouds, for a thousand years, drift on and on in vain.
lines.en: for a thousand years white clouds have drifted by.

lines.py: qíng chuān lì lì hàn yáng shù
lines.lit: Over the sunlit river, clear one by one, the trees of Hanyang;
lines.en: Across the bright river, Hanyang’s trees stand clear;

lines.py: fāng cǎo qī qī yīng wǔ zhōu
lines.lit: fragrant grass grows thick on Parrot Island.
lines.en: sweet grass grows thick on Parrot Island.

lines.py: rì mù xiāng guān hé chù shì
lines.lit: At sunset, where is my home?
lines.en: The sun goes down — which way is home?

lines.py: yān bō jiāng shàng shǐ rén chóu
lines.lit: Mist and waves on the river make one sad.
lines.en: Mist on the river waves fills me with sorrow.

words.en: people of the past (here, the immortal)
words.note: 昔：从前，现代汉语“昔日”“今昔”。
复：再；返：回来。成语“一去不复返”今天仍常用。
载：年，读 zǎi。成语“千载难逢”。

words.en: drifting on and on; long and slow

words.note: 原在武昌城外的长江中，后来被江水冲没。
暮：傍晚，现代汉语“暮色”“朝三暮四”。
江面上雾气笼罩的水波。

imagery.name: 鹤
imagery.zh: 黄鹤代表传说中的仙人，一去不返，写出人去楼空、往事难追。
imagery.en: The yellow crane stands for the legendary immortal: gone for good, it leaves only an empty tower and a past that can’t be recovered.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 千年不变、悠悠飘荡的白云，衬出人世变化和时间的漫长。
imagery.en: White clouds drifting on unchanged for a thousand years set off how much the human world has changed.

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 鹦鹉洲上茂盛的芳草，是眼前的美景，也勾起游子的乡愁。
imagery.en: Lush grass on Parrot Island is a lovely sight — and, as so often in Chinese poems, it stirs a traveller’s longing for home.

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 暮色中烟雾茫茫的江面，看不清家乡的方向，带来无边的愁绪。
imagery.en: The misty river at dusk hides the way home and fills the poet with endless sorrow.
